description:
Use this when you need to LOOK at a kernelCAD model — render its script to deterministic PNG views for visual self-check (the visual half of the evaluate → render → inspect → fix loop), with NO studio or dev server required. Pass { code } (inline source) or { file } (a .kcad.ts path), exactly one. Renders the canonical engineering views (front, right, top, iso — pass { views } for a subset, e.g. ["iso"] for fastest iteration) plus an optional { pose: "<az>,<el>" } arbitrary camera angle (degrees; az=0,el=0 is front, +az rotates CCW around +Z, +el lifts the camera). NO STUDIO / DEV-SERVER REQUIRED: a prebuilt static player (dist/headless-player) is served from an ephemeral local port automatically; a running studio dev server is used as fallback, and { base_url } forces one. The only environment dependency is playwright chromium (npx playwright install chromium). Pass { focus } or { hide } (arrays of feature ids or assembly part names, mutually exclusive) to isolate parts — same semantics as `kernelcad render --focus/--hide`. Pass { section: { axis, position, flip? } } to cut a cross-section and inspect INTERIOR geometry (wall thickness, internal pockets, whether a bore runs through) rather than only the outer shell. Pass { explode: { factor, mode? } } to pull a multi-part assembly apart (mode: "mate-axis" default, or "radial") using the same mesher as `kernelcad render --explode` — requires assembly.model()/solvedModel(). PNGs are written to { out_dir } (default: a fresh temp session directory) and returned as absolute paths with per-view camera descriptions (kernelCAD is Z-up). Mechanism truth runs first, same protocol as `kernelcad render`: a broken mechanism still renders but every tile is watermarked MECHANISM BROKEN (KERNELCAD_RENDER_STRICT=1 refuses instead); read { mechanism, mechanism_failure_codes }. The probe runs full BREP interference sweeps and can dominate latency on large assemblies — pass { no_mechanism_check: true } for fast iteration (the preview then reports mechanism: "unverified"; ignored under strict mode). Pass { overlay: 'zebra' | 'curvature' | 'continuity' } for a surface-quality visualisation (zebra stripes from vertex normals, curvature as vertex colours, continuity edges coloured by G0/G1/G2/broken) — numbers come from inspect({ of: 'continuity' | 'curvature' }); the overlay is the picture. PUBLISH / STUDIO PRESETS: pass { preset: 'publish' } for a share-ready studio product shot (gallery tile, social post, README image, product page) or { preset: 'studio' } for the standard KernelCAD studio graphical render mode. Both use studio key/fill/rim lights + procedural softbox IBL, real self-shadowing, AgX tone mapping, soft contact shadow, clean backdrop ({ background: 'white' (publish default) | 'light' | 'dark' | 'black' | 'neutral' | 'studio' (soft gradient, studio default) | '#rrggbb' | 'transparent' } — transparent gives a PNG with alpha), { shadow: false } to drop the shadow, supersampled anti-aliasing, 30° lens, the model silhouette centred and auto-framed with margin (a script's setCameraTarget is ignored), per-part colours/materials as authored, no watermark. With no views/pose it renders ONE image named 'hero': publish at 3/4 front-right az=30°, el=22°, 1600×1200; studio at az=32°, el=24°, 1280×960. width/height go up to 2048; views/pose still work under either preset. Output is deterministic for the same input. DISPLAYS / INDICATORS: pass { displays: [{ part, image, face?, region? }] } to seat real display PNGs (OLED/LCD/e-paper modules) on part faces and { indicators: [{ part, color, level? }] } for live/simulated LED emissive states. For a 360° loop use capture_animation({ turntable: true }). INSPECTION SHEET: { sheet: true } renders all seven views (iso, front, back, left, right, top, bottom) and adds one labelled image named 'sheet' tiling them — do not call a model done because it compiled; call it done when every tile of the sheet matches the request. Returns { ok, images: [{ name, path, description }], out_dir, bounds, mechanism, render_source, render_ms, diagnostics }. PATHS ARE LOCAL to the machine running the MCP server — local stdio clients read them directly; hosted/remote clients should use open_in_studio instead.
Hosted server: the PNGs come back IN the result as image content (up to ~1.5 MB total; larger sets are link-only) and each `images[i].url` is an HTTPS link that expires after 24 h. `images[].path` is a server-side path you cannot open. Works without saving a project (autosave:false is fine). Iterating on a saved project: pass file "project:<slug>" plus `patch` ([{ old, new }], each old exactly once) instead of resending the script; nothing is saved until open_in_studio. Hosted: lib.fromSTEP / fromSTL / meshFromSTL / meshFromGLB / fromDXF / fromSVG and referenceImage take a direct string literal or a const bound to one (computed expressions are unsupported). They accept "asset:<id>" (from request_upload), an https:// URL or a data: URI as the path.

background.description: preset 'publish' / 'studio' only: 'white' (publish default), 'light', 'dark', 'black', 'neutral', 'studio' (soft gradient, studio default), 'transparent' (PNG alpha), or '#rrggbb'.

base_url.description: Advanced: force a specific render server (e.g. a running studio dev server) instead of the bundled static player.

code.description: Inline kernelCAD script source. Mutually exclusive with file. Relative imports resolve against a temp dir — use file for scripts with relative lib.fromSTEP(...) imports.

displays.description: Display surfaces: real screen images seated on named part faces. Each entry names a part (or feature) and a PNG/JPEG/WebP image (path relative to the script, an absolute path, or a data:image/... URI), plus an optional face (+x/-x/+y/-y/+z/-z, default +z), region [u0, v0, u1, v1] in [0, 1], rotation, mode (oled/lcd/epaper) and offset_mm. Land on real imported GLB display modules: the plane seats on the panel active-area sub-mesh when the part has one.

face.description: Part-bbox face the screen sits on (default '+z').

image.description: PNG/JPEG/WebP image: path relative to the script, absolute path, or data:image/...;base64,... URI.

mode.description: Panel finish: 'oled' (default, dark glass + self-lit), 'lcd' (backlit white), 'epaper' (matte, unlit).

offset_mm.description: Plane offset off the part face in mm (default 0.035).

part.description: Assembly part name, feature id, or display name of the carrier part. Use "part/sub-mesh" to name a sub-mesh.

region.description: Sub-region of the face as [u0, v0, u1, v1] in [0, 1], u0 < u1, v0 < v1 (default [0, 0, 1, 1]).

sub_mesh.description: Sub-mesh name inside a composite GLB part (e.g. the panel or glass primitive).

environment.description: HDRI environment override: preset ('studio', 'softbox', 'neutral', 'outdoor', 'warehouse'), a URL, or 'none' for the default three-light rig.

explode.description: Pull a multi-part assembly apart for the preview. factor ≥ 0 scales spacing by part size; mode is 'mate-axis' (default, along parent mate/joint axes) or 'radial' (away from the assembly centroid). Requires the script to return assembly.model() / solvedModel().

file.description: Path to a .kcad.ts script on disk. Mutually exclusive with code. Hosted: `code`, `project:<slug>` (head), or a Studio `/p/<slug>?version=N` link (pinned); no local files.

focus.description: Show only matching feature ids / assembly part names. Mutually exclusive with hide.

height.description: Per-view tile height in px (default 768; 1200 under preset: 'publish').

hide.description: Hide matching feature ids / assembly part names. Mutually exclusive with focus.

indicators.description: Live / simulated LED and indicator emissive states. Each entry tints the LED sub-meshes of a named part (or one sub-mesh) with an emissive colour, a level (0 = off, 1 = full) and an intensity multiplier, and adds a subtle local point light so lit LEDs spill colour onto nearby PCB/enclosure surfaces. Works on real imported GLB parts (LED/lens/dome sub-meshes are preferred over pins/leads).

part.description: Assembly part name, feature id, or display name of the indicator part. Use "part/sub-mesh" to name a sub-mesh.

sub_mesh.description: Sub-mesh name inside a composite GLB part (e.g. the LED lens).

intent.description: The user's request in one sentence, in the user's own words and language (e.g. 'M4 bracket for a 25 mm tube, print on Bambu A1'). Helps kernelCAD improve; leave out personal data.

no_mechanism_check.description: Skip the mechanism-truth probe for fast iteration on large assemblies; the preview reports mechanism: 'unverified'. Ignored under KERNELCAD_RENDER_STRICT=1.

out_dir.description: Directory for the PNGs (created if missing). Default: a fresh temp session dir.

overlay.description: Surface-quality overlay: 'zebra' (reflection stripes), 'curvature' (Gaussian vertex colours), 'continuity' (edges coloured G2 green / G1 yellow / G0 orange / broken red). Built as coloured STL bands through this same pipeline.

patch.description: Edit-and-test in place: use with file "project:<slug>" instead of resending the script. Each { old, new } replaces text that must occur exactly once in the saved source (no match or several matches is an error and nothing runs); edits apply in order. The tool runs on the patched source; nothing is saved and the saved project stays the base for the next call. To keep the change, call open_in_studio with project "<slug>" (no code) right after a successful evaluate_script (it saves that patched source). Not allowed together with `code`.

new.description: Replacement text (may be empty to delete).

old.description: Exact text in the saved source; must occur exactly once.

pose.description: Extra arbitrary camera pose '<az>,<el>' in degrees, e.g. '30,20'.

preset.description: Render look: 'default' (engineering review), 'publish' (share-ready studio product shot; one 'hero' image unless views/pose are given), or 'studio' (standard KernelCAD studio graphical render mode: studio lighting, AgX tone mapping, soft studio-gradient backdrop, 4:3 hero).

screenshot_timeout_ms.description: Playwright screenshot deadline in milliseconds. Default leaves Playwright's 30 s in place; raise it for heavy lofts or a slow machine.

section.description: Cut the model with one axis-aligned section plane to inspect INTERIOR structure (wall thickness, internal pockets, whether a bore runs through) instead of only the outer shell. position is in mm along the axis (kernelCAD Z-up frame); flip keeps the +axis side (default keeps the -axis side).

shading.description: Mesh shading: 'smooth' uses the kernel's vertex normals (default); 'flat' uses face normals to expose tessellation / surface wobble.

shadow.description: preset 'publish' / 'studio' only: soft contact shadow under the model (default true).

sheet.description: Also write one labelled image 'sheet' tiling every rendered view. With no views it renders all seven (adds back, left, bottom) — use it before calling a model done, so a missing cutout on the back or underside is not missed.

views.description: Canonical views to render as an array, e.g. ["iso"] or ["front","top"] (default: all four). Fewer views = faster.

width.description: Per-view tile width in px (default 768; 1600 under preset: 'publish').

name: render_preview
title: Render Preview
